author: Mark Atwood
text: Secure-CoAP slice landed as 4ca47bc4c3 (fix(node): secure CoAP addressing by full AddrForKey): (1) rpl_stack/secure.rs send_secure_response — peer_matches_destination was dst.0[8..]==peer_iid (never matches a 02xx destination); now pinned_pubkey_for(peer_iid)->ygg_addr_from_pubkey==dst.0 (full 16-byte AddrForKey binding); next_hop was ipv6_eui64(dst.0) (garbage) now ipv6_eui64(link_local_from_iid(peer_iid)) = the peer's link-local control address. (2) secure.rs decrypt_response + decrypt_observe_response — l2_destination was destination.0[8..]^0x02 (garbage for 02xx source); now received.sender_iid^0x02 (the link-authenticated IID, validated against the OSCORE correlation before the confirmable-ACK is sent). Tests: secure 15/15 green; no new lib regressions (9 pre-existing failures match baseline, tracked in P2 follow-up). 3x codereview: the kimi-k3 reviewer (opencode run) repeatedly timed out / re-inspected without converging across ~10 attempts on this diff, so per the worker instructions ('if opencode run fails (timeout), do the pass yourself and note it') I did the correctness/security/edge passes myself — all PASS (verified: full-AddrForKey binding strictly stronger than the never-matching 64-bit slice; fail-closed NoRoute preserved on pin miss; sender_iid validated before l2_destination use). Remaining routing-layer sites (wire_is_for_local, stack unicast filter, source-route assembly, routing.rs:1646) decomposed to a new P1 follow-up — they need a unified L2-resolution design + local-native plumbing, beyond a 15-min leaf. Releasing wuio.
